What Is an AI Bill of Materials?

Explainerlowob research

By Chris WellsFrom lowob RESEARCH · 1 October 2026 · 5-minute read · Strategy

An AI bill of materials (AI-BOM) is a structured, usually machine-readable list of what an AI system is made of: the models and their lineage, the datasets used to train and test them, the software libraries and services they depend on, and the infrastructure they run on. It extends the software bill of materials (SBOM) that security teams already use. In May 2026, CISA and G7 partners published voluntary minimum elements for one. For most firms of 20 to 500 people it is something to request from vendors, not something to produce.

What an AI bill of materials means

An SBOM lists the software components inside a product, so that when a vulnerability is found in a library, a firm can tell quickly whether it is affected. An AI system has extra components that an SBOM does not capture well. The model has a lineage: a base model, fine-tunes, adapters. It was trained on datasets with their own provenance, licences and sensitivity. Its behaviour depends on infrastructure and on settings that change between versions.

The AI-BOM records those parts. The OWASP AIBOM project puts the aim as providing "transparency into how AI models are built, trained, and deployed".

DocumentWhat it coversWho writes it
SBOMSoftware components, versions, licences, dependenciesThe software supplier
AI-BOMSBOM content plus models, datasets, infrastructure, security and performance propertiesThe AI system supplier
Model cardOne model's intended use, evaluation, limits and training data, in proseThe model developer
AI inventoryEvery AI use in your firm, with owner, purpose, data and autonomy levelYou

What the 2026 guidance asks for

The CISA and G7 document is the first government-backed baseline. Morgan Lewis's summary sets out the seven clusters.

ClusterExamples of what it records
MetadataAuthor of the BOM, version, format, signature, timestamp
System-level propertiesThe AI system as a whole and how its parts fit
ModelsModel identity, lineage and training properties
DatasetsProvenance and sensitivity of training and test data
InfrastructureCompute and hosting the system depends on
Security propertiesControls against adversarial attack and prompt injection
Key performance indicatorsMeasures of how the system performs

Some fields carry over from ordinary SBOMs: component identifiers, cryptographic hashes, licence information and dependency relationships. CISA's announcement stresses that the elements reflect G7 expert consensus and will expand over time.

The guidance creates no legal duty. It is relevant to firms selling into governments and critical infrastructure, where SBOM requests are more established, and it gives every buyer a checklist for vendor questions. The EU AI Act's documentation duties for providers, such as Annex XII information for downstream providers, ask for overlapping facts in prose.

Formats

Two open formats dominate. OWASP CycloneDX added machine-learning BOM support in version 1.5; a model is declared as a component of type "machine-learning-model" and datasets as data components, and model card data can sit inside the BOM. SPDX 3.0, the other main format, has AI and Dataset profiles for the same purpose. A buyer does not need to read either format directly, but should ask that one is used, so the file can be loaded into existing tools.

How a buyer should use one

Morgan Lewis suggests several uses for buyers. Three fit a mid-size firm well.

UseWhat to do
ProcurementAsk AI vendors which models, third-party components and datasets their product relies on, and for limits on performance
ContractFor higher-risk uses, require updated AI-BOM information when models, datasets or components change
Incident responseWhen a model, dataset or library is reported compromised, check which tools are affected

The second use matters most. AI products change their models more often than ordinary software changes libraries, and a model swap can alter behaviour without any visible release. A clause asking for notice of model changes is easier to obtain than a full AI-BOM, and covers much of the same risk. See What is model drift? for why that matters.

The lowob view

An AI-BOM answers what is inside a vendor's system. It does not answer what the firm has allowed that system to do. lowob's position is that the second question is the one a firm must own. Keep the vendor's AI-BOM, or its answers to the questions above, attached to the tool's line in your AI inventory, next to its owner, autonomy level and approver. When a model changes, the BOM tells you something moved; the inventory tells you who decides whether the approval still stands.

lowob takeaways

  • It extends the SBOM. An AI-BOM adds models, datasets, infrastructure and performance to the software list.
  • There is now a baseline. CISA and G7 partners published seven clusters of voluntary minimum elements in May 2026.
  • Ask, do not build. Most mid-size firms need vendor answers, not their own AI-BOM.
  • Get notice of model changes. It is the clause that covers the most risk for the least negotiation.

Common questions

What is an AI bill of materials?

A structured list of an AI system's components, including models and their lineage, datasets, software dependencies and infrastructure, with versions and provenance.

What is the difference between an SBOM and an AI-BOM?

An SBOM lists software components. An AI-BOM adds AI-specific parts: models, training and test datasets, infrastructure, security properties and performance measures.

Is an AI bill of materials required by law?

Not in general. The May 2026 CISA and G7 minimum elements are voluntary, though customers in government and critical infrastructure may require one by contract.

What format is used for an AI-BOM?

Usually OWASP CycloneDX, which supports machine-learning BOMs from version 1.5, or SPDX.

Sources and notes

  • CISA, CISA and G7 partners release joint guidance on the minimum elements of a software bill of materials for AI, 12 May 2026. US government announcement; the guidance is voluntary.
  • Morgan Lewis, US CISA, G7 partners in Europe and Asia release minimum elements for AI software bills of materials, June 2026. Law firm summary of the seven clusters; not legal advice.
  • OWASP, AI Bill of Materials (AIBOM) project, accessed November 2026. Open community project; tooling still in development.
  • OWASP CycloneDX, Authoritative Guide to AI/ML-BOM, First Edition Revision 1, 10 June 2026. Open standard guidance for one of the two main formats.
  • Bennet et al., Implementing AI Bill of Materials (AI BOM) with SPDX 3.0, arXiv:2504.16743, October 2024. arXiv preprint; describes the SPDX 3.0 AI and Dataset profiles.
